name: datapath
description: The selector, memory and random types wired into one clocked circuit, consuming each other and feeding the flat kinds, with no input. A CLK (period 2, halt link0 undriven) drives clk=link1; a NOT of the undriven link2 gives one=link3 (high from tick 1). A 2-bit JK counter: q0=link4 (J=K=one), q1=link6 (J=K=q0). An RNG on clk draws r0..r3=links 12-15 on each rising edge. DEC(q0,q1) -> one-hot links 8-11; each output gates its r bit through an AND2 onto the shared bus link28 (four drivers: invalid whenever the selected bit is high). MUX(select q0,q1; data r0..r3) -> m=link16; DEMUX(select q0,q1; data m) -> links 17-20; ENC with valid over those -> bits links 21/22, valid link23. RAM (address q0,q1; data links 24/25; WE=m; clk) -> links 26/27, whose data inputs are XOR2s of its own outputs with r0/r1 (read-modify-write feedback through the RAM). XOR2(bus, m) -> link29 shows the one-tick skew between the DEC/AND path and the MUX. A D flip-flop latches the ENC valid on clk -> links 30/31; a D flip-flop with D and clock both on one latches high on the power-on edge -> links 32/33; an SR (S=ENC valid, enable clk, R=ENC bit0) enters the invalid state on an edge where the ENC reads an odd value, leaves it on an even valid one and holds it while nothing is valid -> links 34/35; a 3-input AND(q0, q1, m) -> link36.
